correctness.rationale: For E ordinary and Y elliptic, the actual restricted-power Jacobson formula yields T(f)=f^p+delta^(p-1)f-hf. Riemann--Roch and the exact residue map produce a basis 1,f_1,...,f_(d-1) with T(f_j)=0 via p-divisibility of Pic^0(Y) and the logarithmic derivative identity. The equality T(c+sum b_j f_j)=(c^p-hc)+sum(b_j^p-b_j) f_j^p, together with independence of 1,f_j^p, proves the coefficient scheme ideal. Exact-pole open conditions select precisely the nonzero zero-sum residue vectors, giving the claimed alpha_p or constant F_p components, length and point count in every prime/d. The included CHECK.py finite checks ran successfully but are not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact finite scheme fibers over reduced divisors of the p-closed turbulent foliation locus are a natural moduli invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice: the pole divisor is the projection used in the source moduli construction. Scheme lengths and geometric point counts distinguish ordinary and supersingular Y (etale F_p versus infinitesimal alpha_p), a phenomenon invisible to pointwise existence criteria. The result classifies all reduced divisors in every characteristic and has potential use in degeneration/stratification of the global p-closed foliation locus.
